chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Convenience as addiction; Ichabod Crane
summary: A conversation on sterile planned communities and convenience as an addiction, then a tangent about Ichabod Crane.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: That was, what you're saying reminds me of something I saw on television last night. And I'll say this very quickly but it's so supportive of what you're saying. There was an ideal community thing

shown and everything the people needed was right there. The playgrounds for the children, the shopping centers, the recreation areas for adults. Every single thing was right there. And I thought, how sterile, how terrible. And what these people are missing by not having interaction with other people. Not getting out of their own little circumscribed world.
And I'm so really glad to hear you say what you did because I certainly share your thinking on that.
Well the worse addication in the world is never even mentioned that's convenience. That's one of the world's worse addications. (LAUGHTER).
You come out with such marvellous statements, you really do. You know, as I told you, and I'll just mention, you have this kind of Ichabod Crane quality.
We were trying to figure out who Ichabod Crane was when you said that the other day and you said it and we were trying to figure it out.
First, we thought it was the one who slept twenty years. But that was Rip Van Winkle.
Rip Van Winkle (LAUGHTER). No, he was the old school teacher.
Oh, a school teacher? whose writing was......
I looked up Ichabod in the dictionary and it said that it was a name, a persons name. But it didn't say anything................ (VOICE FADES OUT).

No, marvellous. And old New England school teacher. And you see, it's so clear to me that you have thought so deeply about so many things and it has come out as we've talked you know, here and there that you..........
